title: 3 · Performance deep-dive
description: Simulator, Kafka processing and lag, transactions, gRPC, database, disk and memory. Panels named after Kafka Streams / JDBC / JVM figures show the Hub's Python equivalents; each panel's description says what it measures. Broker panels need the JMX exporter on the kafka service; broker-side lag needs kafka-exporter (obs profile).

panels.title: E2E Latency (Simulator)
panels.description: M1 sent to M2 received, timed by the ESS: from the moment it starts HubInbound.Deliver* (playing FIN / SnF inbound) to the moment the Hub's SendMt / SendMx reaches the emulated network for the same UETR. Includes the edge and every gRPC hop. Format and flow are the inbound side (M1).

panels.title: M1 sent (Simulator), M2 received (Simulator)
panels.description: M1: inbound messages the ESS delivered and the Hub accepted. M2: outbound messages the Hub sent to the emulated FIN / SnF. Unmatched M2s are repeats (the Hub retrying a send) with no M1 waiting. The gap between the lines is work in flight inside the Hub.

panels.title: E2E Latency
panels.description: The Hub's own end-to-end histogram, T0 (network delivery) to T6 (COMPLETED on the network ACK), observed by the ACK matcher. Compare with the simulator's view on the left.

panels.title: Consumer Lag (Consumer)
panels.description: Lag at read, reported by each stage: log end minus the offset just read. Only updates when a stage reads, so a stuck stage keeps its last value — use the broker view next to it for that.

panels.title: Consumer Lag (Broker)
panels.description: Committed offset against log end, read from the cluster by kafka-exporter (obs profile). Keeps moving while a consumer is stuck or down. Clamped at 0: on transactional topics the exporter can read the log end before the committed offset and briefly report a negative lag.

panels.title: Streams processed records per second
panels.description: Records each stage processed (state-topic records excluded), by outcome. retry / dlq are records sent down the retry ladder.

panels.title: Listener consumed records per second
panels.description: Every record each consumer group read, the compacted hub.pay.state included.

panels.title: Broker records in per sec
panels.description: MessagesInPerSec per topic, from the broker's JMX exporter. Sizing only: one payment is several records on several topics, so this is not TPS.

panels.title: Broker records in total
panels.description: Cumulative records appended per topic since the broker started (resets with the broker: no named volumes locally).

panels.title: Broker bytes in per sec
panels.description: BytesInPerSec per topic. Raw MT/MX travel only on *.raw topics (claim-check), so those dominate.

panels.title: Broker bytes out per sec
panels.description: BytesOutPerSec per topic: every consumer group reading a topic multiplies it.

panels.title: Streams commit latency average
panels.description: producer.commit per stage: send_offsets_to_transaction plus commit_transaction, i.e. the client side of one read-process-write transaction.

panels.title: Broker prepare to complete average
panels.description: WriteTxnMarkers: the transaction coordinator writing COMMIT markers to every partition in the transaction, the PrepareCommit to CompleteCommit phase. EndTxn is the client's commit request as the broker times it. Broker mean (exponentially decaying), in ms.

panels.title: Commit per second
panels.description: Committed and aborted transactions per stage. One commit is one batch.

panels.title: Streams commit latency max
panels.description: Longest commit per stage over the last 30-60 s.

panels.title: Broker prepare to complete max
panels.description: Broker-side Max of the same two requests.

panels.title: Broker errors
panels.description: Request errors by API and error code (error=NONE, the success count, excluded), plus failed produce / fetch requests.

panels.title: Process latency avg
panels.description: Time to process one record in a stage, excluding the commit: parse, screen, route, dispatch, including any outbound gRPC call. 'post-commit' is work done after the commit, per batch: the DB sink's PostgreSQL write.

panels.title: Rebalance
panels.description: Partition assignment changes per consumer group since the process started (a step up is a rebalance), and the partitions each group holds now. Cumulative rather than increase(): Prometheus cannot see a counter's first value, and the first rebalance happens at startup.

panels.title: Process Total
panels.description: Records processed since each process started, by stage and outcome.

panels.title: Process latency max
panels.description: Longest single-record processing time per stage over the last 30-60 s, and the longest post-commit step (the DB sink's write, per batch).

panels.title: Poll time
panels.description: Time inside one consumer poll. Bounded by the poll timeout when a stage is idle, so a high average with low lag just means quiet.

panels.title: IO Wait Ratio
panels.description: Share of each stage thread's wall clock spent waiting for records (polling plus idle back-off). Near 1 = idle; falling towards 0 = the stage is saturated and processing back to back.

panels.title: gRPC client calls (outbound)
panels.description: Calls made, per attempt: a retried call counts once per attempt, as the network sees it. Hub → FIN / SnF / compliance service, and ESS → Hub.

panels.title: gRPC client call duration (outbound)
panels.description: Per attempt. Deadlines: Deliver* 200 ms, Send* 500 ms, Screen 1 s.

panels.title: gRPC server calls (inbound)
panels.description: Calls served: HubInbound / HubNetworkEvents / HubCompliance on the Hub, FinGateway / SnfGateway / ComplianceScreening on the ESS. The ESS control API (EssControl) is excluded.

panels.title: gRPC server call duration (inbound)
panels.description: Served-call latency. Deliver* replies only after the acks=all Kafka write.

panels.title: JDBC idle connections
panels.description: The Hub is Python, so this is the DB sink's PostgreSQL connection (psycopg), not a JDBC pool. Connections it holds: idle between batches, active during a write. The sink keeps one connection; zero means it is not connected (dry-run, or reconnecting after an error).

panels.title: JDBC Calls
panels.description: The DB sink's PostgreSQL calls (psycopg). Statements and transaction calls per second, by operation and outcome: upsert and audit_insert per status event, commit per batch.

panels.title: Kafka disk usage
panels.description: Log size per topic on the broker, all partitions (kafka.log Size).

panels.title: Kafka streams Disk usage per instance
panels.description: The Kafka Streams 'disk usage per instance' equivalent. The Hub's state store is in memory (rebuilt from hub.pay.state), so this is an estimate of the bytes it holds, per process and stage.

panels.title: Kafka stream number of keys per instance
panels.description: The Hub's state store (in memory, rebuilt from hub.pay.state), in place of a Kafka Streams RocksDB store. Working keys (payments in flight, HELD, cover legs waiting) and the bounded window of completed UETRs kept for de-duplication.

panels.title: Used Memory - Old Gen
panels.description: Kafka broker JVM. The old-generation pool: G1 Old Gen, or Tenured Gen when the JVM picks Serial GC (it does below ~1.8 GB of container memory, as locally). A sawtooth is healthy; a floor that keeps rising is not.

panels.title: Used Memory - Heap
panels.description: Kafka broker JVM heap (-Xmx1g locally) against its committed and max size.

panels.title: Used Memory - Non-Heap
panels.description: Kafka broker JVM: metaspace, code cache and compressed class space.

panels.title: Full GC Pauses
panels.description: Kafka broker JVM. Time per second in old-generation (full) collections, and how many ran in the last minute (G1 Old Generation, or MarkSweepCompact under Serial GC). Young collections are shown for scale.

panels.title: Used Memory - Resident (RSS)
panels.description: Python has no heap / old-gen split; the resident set is the figure the container's mem_limit is enforced against.

panels.title: Allocated blocks
panels.description: Memory blocks the interpreter has allocated (sys.getallocatedblocks). Steady growth under steady load is a leak.

panels.title: Virtual memory
panels.description: Address space reserved by each process.

panels.title: Full GC Pauses (generation 2)
panels.description: Stop-the-world time per second in generation-2 collections, the Python full GC, and the p99 single pause.
